children: Australian shares ended slightly lower on Wednesday as losses in financials outweighed gains in miners, while caution over oil-driven inflation kept investors focused on the risk of tighter monetary policy.
closed 0.1% lower at 8,911.40, its lowest since July 27, after swinging between gains and losses.

Australian stocks carried a risk-off mood into a second session, with elevated oil prices, rising bond yields and a more hawkish rate outlook keeping investors on edge, said Hebe Chen, a market analyst at Vantage Markets.

Reserve Bank of Australia Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said on Tuesday the monetary policy board would debate the case for a rate hike at its next meeting, citing stubborn inflation and upside risks.
Markets priced in a 74% chance of a rate hike to 4.6% at the September 29 meeting, up from 67% a day earlier.
